preheader: Tech's massive AI funding push, Boeing drops on delays, and PwC on new entry-level skill demands.

lead.headline: Tech companies take on heavy debt and stock sales to fund AI expansion
lead.body: Major tech companies are borrowing hundreds of billions of dollars and selling new stock to pay for data centers and specialized chips. Companies are relying on complex financing structures to secure cash as capital demands continue to climb.
lead.why: Understanding how massive infrastructure projects get financed gives you direct insight into modern corporate balance sheets and venture debt.

stories.headline: Boeing shares tumble after CEO reports 737 Max production delays
stories.body: Boeing stock fell nearly 10% on Tuesday after CEO Kelly Ortberg announced during an earnings call that the aircraft manufacturer will miss its monthly production rate targets for the 737 Max.
stories.why: Manufacturing delays directly hit cash flow and delivery schedules, serving as a real-time study in corporate operations.

stories.headline: American Airlines raises rewards credit card fee for first time since 2018
stories.body: American Airlines and Citi raised the annual fee on their co-branded Platinum Select card from $99 to $150. The card added new perks such as a TSA PreCheck credit and additional points on hotel stays to offset the increase.
stories.why: Companies use bundled benefits to protect customer retention when raising prices on recurring financial products.

stories.headline: Google DeepMind unveils Genie 4 world model
stories.body: DeepMind introduced Genie 4, an upgraded world model designed to generate realistic physics and human movements. The model will roll out soon to developers and Google AI Ultra subscribers.
stories.why: World models allow software to simulate real-world environments, creating new opportunities for startups building autonomous systems.

stories.headline: Anthropic IPO filings reveal confidential founder voting arrangement
stories.body: Seven Anthropic cofounders holding 50.1% of voting control can confidentially name up to 10 successors in a special LLC to inherit their voting power.
stories.why: Corporate governance structures reveal how startup founders protect long-term control before going public.

stories.headline: PwC finds AI-exposed entry-level jobs increasingly require senior skills
stories.body: A PwC analysis of 2.4 million entry-level US roles revealed that junior jobs exposed to AI are 7 times more likely to require skills traditionally expected of senior employees, such as leadership.
stories.why: As automation handles basic tasks, you will need to demonstrate higher-level decision skills earlier in your career.

stories.headline: McKinsey report tracks agentic AI potential and obstacles in banking
stories.body: McKinsey found that agentic AI can cut bank verification process times by 30% to 70%. However, high human oversight costs and governance challenges continue to slow wider corporate adoption.
stories.why: Consultants advise corporate clients on how to weigh technological efficiency against operational risk.

stories.headline: Orange County DA agrees to expunge profiles from DNA database
stories.body: The Orange County District Attorney's office settled a lawsuit by agreeing to remove profiles from its controversial DNA database. A UC Irvine criminology professor who filed the lawsuit in 2021 called the decision an important step forward.

stories.headline: Venus Williams falls to 0-13 in singles this year
stories.body: Venus Williams lost 6-2, 6-2 to 18-year-old Lilli Tagger at the Guangzhou Open on Tuesday. The defeat drops the 46-year-old former Grand Slam champion to 0-13 in singles matches for the season.

term.name: Agentic AI
term.definition: Artificial intelligence systems capable of executing multi-step workflows autonomously with minimal human intervention. In banking, McKinsey notes these agents can cut background checks by 30% to 70%, though human oversight costs still slow adoption.

serve.headline: General Compute raised $100M to challenge Nvidia in AI inference
serve.body: San Francisco startup General Compute raised $100 million in Series A funding to build an AI inference cloud using non-Nvidia chips from Cerebras, SambaNova, and Positron AI. The company aims to run AI applications faster and cheaper than standard GPUs.
